source_title: Ban on construction, demolition activities in Delhi-NCR from November 5-20: Union Minister
source_excerpt: Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bhupender Yadav on Friday (October 30, 2026) announced that there will be a ban on construction and demolition activities in Delhi and NCR from November 5 to 20, with some exemptions. Only 40-60% of actions to fight air pollution completed so far in Delhi, nearby States Only 40-60% of actions to fight air pollution completed so far in Delhi, nearby States Despite the air quality of Delhi and many other cities in the region already worsening to the “poor” and “very poor” levels, many actions to reduce air pollution are yet to be completed Only 40-60% of actions to fight air pollution completed so far in Delhi, nearby States storyline 1 The Commission for Air Quality Management in the National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) will issue an order on Friday (October 30, 2026), the Minister said. While GRAP 1 remains in force, the CAQM is enforcing additional measures to make the overall actions on the air pollution in the region even more stricter. https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Delhi/grap-1-curbs-imposed-in-delhi-ncr-as-air-quality-slips-into-poor-category/article71607093.ece How is air pollution in Delhi-NCR ahead of winter? storyline 1 “This is our peak time (for air pollution). This will be for dust generating demolition and outdoor civil construction activities,” he said, adding that exemption will be given for projects of national importance. CAQM directs States to focus on vehicular pollution, stubble burning CAQM directs States to focus on vehicular pollution, stubble burning The CAQM also directed the agencies to focus on strengthening inspection and compliance-monitoring mechanisms across the NCR CAQM directs States to focus on vehicular pollution, stubble burning storyline 1 Earlier in June, the Delhi government issued a gazette notification banning dust generating demolition activity and outdoor civil construction activity in the city from November 1 to January 31. Exemption was given to essential public infrastructure projects. Such a fixed period ban on construction activities is not a usual measure taken by the CAQM. A senior official told The Hindu that this measure is being taken, considering that Deepavali is on November 8 and pollution from firecrackers is expected to increase. Also, pollution from stubble burning in the region is expected to peak around the same time, as harvesting is also underway, the official added. As per the June gazette notification by the Delhi government, 50% work from home is mandatory for government and private offices in Delhi from November 1 to January 31 , with some exemptions.
